title: Capcom confirms data breach that affected 11.7 million users

claims.claim: Capcom confirmed a data breach that affected 11.7 million users.

evidence.quote: Capcom confirms data breach that affected 11.7 million users

claims.claim: The data breach included account emails, birth dates, genders, countries or regions, and nicknames of 43 accounts.

evidence.quote: the data breach included millions of account emails, but also the birth date, gender, country or region and nicknames of 43 accounts
According to Capcom's statement, the data breach included millions of account emails, but also the birth date, gender, country or region and nicknames of 43 accounts

claims.claim: Unauthorized changes were made to 196 account passwords.

evidence.quote: as well as unauthorized changes to 196 account passwords.

claims.claim: Customer credit card information was not included in the data breach.

evidence.quote: However, the company noted that customer credit card information was not included in this data breach.

claims.claim: The incident began on October 19 when suspicious activity was detected on Capcom ID.

evidence.quote: Capcom said the incident began on October 19 when it "detected suspicious activity indicating potential unauthorized access" to Capcom ID.

claims.claim: Capcom reported the incident to local police and its external advisory board for security oversight.

evidence.quote: Afterwards, Capcom reported the incident to local police and its external advisory board for security oversight.

claims.claim: Games like Street Fighter 6 still require Capcom ID for online play.

evidence.quote: including games like Street Fighter 6 that require it for online play.

claims.claim: Rockstar Games confirmed in April that it was hit by a third-party data breach.

evidence.quote: as Rockstar Games confirmed in April that it was hit by a "third-party data breach."
